name: Spontaneous Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia

criteria.description: Platelet count fall >50% from baseline or nadir <150 x 10^9/L
Development of HIT-like syndrome without prior heparin exposure
Presence of platelet factor 4 (PF4)-heparin antibodies detected by ELISA or functional assay
New onset arterial or venous thrombosis
Exclusion of other causes of thrombocytopenia and thrombosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of thrombocytopenia with >50% platelet count fall, positive PF4 antibody test, and absence of prior heparin exposure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires high clinical suspicion and confirmation by laboratory testing due to rarity and overlap with other thrombotic microangiopathies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe thrombocytopenia with platelet count <50 x 10^9/L
Spontaneous venous thrombosis without heparin exposure
searchTerms: blood clots in veins without heparin
clot formation without blood thinner exposure

laboratory: Marked thrombocytopenia with platelet count often <50 x 10^9/L
Positive PF4-heparin antibody ELISA and serotonin release assay
Elevated D-dimer and fibrin degradation products
imaging: Ultrasound or CT evidence of venous or arterial thrombosis
MRI or CT for cerebral infarction or venous sinus thrombosis
other: Absence of prior heparin exposure despite HIT-like syndrome
Rapid platelet count recovery after immunomodulatory treatment

distinguishingFeatures: History of heparin exposure within 5-10 days
Typical timing of thrombocytopenia onset after heparin
Absence of spontaneous HIT without heparin
Recurrent thrombosis with or without thrombocytopenia

redFlags: Rapid onset severe thrombocytopenia without heparin exposure
New arterial or venous thrombosis in absence of anticoagulant therapy
Skin necrosis or limb ischemia without trauma
references: Warkentin TE. Spontaneous heparin-induced thrombocytopenia syndrome: an autoimmune disorder with severe thrombosis. Blood. 2014;124(23):3360-3363.
Greinacher A, et al. Autoimmune heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. J Thromb Haemost. 2017;15(11):2099-2114.
